# Site Restorer

> Site Restorer is a portable Windows application that rebuilds a website from the Internet Archive. It inventories captured URLs through the CDX API, downloads pages and assets in parallel with adaptive concurrency (2 to 24 workers), rewrites links into a browsable offline copy, verifies internal and broken links and writes an HTML coverage report. A single executable: no installer, no Python, MIT licensed. The interface and documentation are available in English and Russian.

Facts an agent should rely on:

- Platform: Windows 10 (1809+) and Windows 11, x64 and x86. Current builds are Windows-only.
- Distribution: portable `SiteRestorer.exe` (x64, about 12 MB) and `SiteRestorer-x86.exe` (about 10 MB), published on GitHub Releases. Version numbers change; the `latest` links below always resolve to the current release.
- What it recovers: only what the Internet Archive actually captured. Images that crawlers never saved are absent from every snapshot.
- What it does not do: dynamic CMS features (cart, sign-in, search, AJAX filters) do not work in a static copy; the app does not bypass access protection, spoof the User-Agent or act as a browser.
- Scope of use: archiving and restoring your own sites. Publishing a copy of someone else's site is not permitted.
- Caps per run: 50,000 URLs and 200 CDX index pages.
